tonight.headline: Coker is unlikely to play, and he's still in your flex at 0.0
body: Bad news first. Adam Schefter reported this morning that Jalen Coker is unlikely to play tonight, and ESPN cut his projection from 13.0 to 0.0. He's still in your flex. With Terry McLaurin officially inactive in London and Justin Jefferson out, three of your five receivers are down. As set, ESPN has you at 111.7 against Aye-Aye's 126.0, a 42% chance.

One move fixes most of it: put Alvin Kamara in the flex. That's worth 10.6 projected points and takes you to about 122. Do it now; if Coker is still there at 18:20 and sits, the slot locks at zero. Everything else is the projection lineup. It's before the inactive lists, so re-check each starter 90 minutes before his kickoff.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Aye-Aye start Tetairoa McMillan (15.9), who becomes Carolina's only established receiver if Coker sits, and Tyler Warren (13.1), who is playing in London now with Keenan Allen inactive. They're leaving Aaron Jones (18.1) on the bench behind Kyren Williams (13.1) in the flex; fixing that adds about 5 to their number.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker active at 16:50 with a projection back above 12.6, or Aye-Aye moving Jones into their flex.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Do it now · the flex locks Sun 18:20 Mexico City with Coker in it
doFirst.title: Start Kamara in the flex; bench Coker
doFirst.subtitle: Schefter says Coker is unlikely to play and ESPN now projects him for 0.0. Your flex is worth nothing as set.

case.label: The news
case.body: Adam Schefter reported on Sunday morning that Coker (quad) is unlikely to play against Detroit (NBC Sports and RotoWire notes, 4 Oct; ESPN's headline reads 'Coker also likely out vs. Lions'). He's still listed questionable and Canales wants to take it to game day (CatCrave, 4 Oct). ESPN moved him from 13.0 to 0.0 overnight, so this is priced: the move follows the projection.

case.label: Why Kamara
case.body: 10.6, the highest projection on your bench (Gordon 9.0, Monangai 8.3). He isn't on the Saints' final report (Saints Wire, 3 Oct). It's a committee: 46.7% of snaps and 10 touches once Etienne left in Week 3, with Miller at 31.1% and CJ Donaldson taking the goal line (Sharp Football). Atlanta allow 3.1 yards a carry to backs, 4th-best. He's the projection's answer, not a good matchup.

case.label: The clock
case.body: If Coker is still in the flex at 18:20 tonight and sits, the slot locks at zero. Kamara plays Monday at 18:15, so the swap costs nothing to make now and can be reversed up to 18:20.

case.label: If Coker is active
case.body: Carolina's inactives come at 16:50. If he's active, look at ESPN's number then: swap back only if it's two or more above Kamara's 10.6. Under that, it's a coin flip on a receiver playing through a quad, and Kamara stays.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Tyler Shough for Kamara, not on the Saints' report. Coker's quarterback, Bryce Young, has no designation.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker plays and outscores Kamara, or Gordon or Monangai outscores Kamara (archive). Free receivers at his level (Meyers 10.8, Malik Washington 10.3) were coin flips and weren't added.

doFirst.sources: NBC Sports · RotoWire · ESPN headline · CatCrave · Saints Wire · Sharp Football · lineup_check.py

whatWentWrong.title: Coker went from 13.0 to 0.0 overnight
whatWentWrong.lead: Saturday's brief said to leave him in the flex until 16:50. By this morning the projection itself says bench him.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Schefter: unlikely to play (NBC Sports and RotoWire notes, 4 Oct). SI's Panthers site had said on Saturday that Canales tied Ja'seem Reed's call-up to Coker not playing; the brief treated that as a hint because Legette's move to IR explained it equally well. The hint was right.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The card above: Kamara into the flex now. And Tuesday: Legette is out at least four games, so Coker returns to a bigger role when the quad heals. He isn't a drop.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker active at 16:50. Then ESPN's updated number decides, by the two-point rule on the card.

whatWentWrong.title: Three of five receivers are down
whatWentWrong.lead: Jefferson out, McLaurin inactive, Coker unlikely. The bench is three running backs and two injured receivers.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Jefferson has no return date and O'Connell won't rush him (Vikings.com, 2 Oct). McLaurin has no timeline. CatCrave expects Coker back after Carolina's bye, which is one writer's read.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing more today: the free receivers (Meyers 10.8, Malik Washington 10.3, Raymond 9.8) are within a coin flip of Kamara's 10.6. On Tuesday, Metcalf and Boston clear waivers and Monangai's seat goes to one of them.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing before Tuesday. Even if Jefferson and McLaurin practise on Wednesday, claims process first, so the claim still goes in.

lineupCheck.verdict: The lineup as set is 10.6 points below the projection lineup: Coker is in the flex at 0.0 and the projection starts Kamara there.

moves.reason: PROJECTION — 10.6 points. This follows the projection rather than overriding it: ESPN cut Coker from 13.0 to 0.0 after Adam Schefter reported on Sunday morning, 4 Oct, that he is unlikely to play.

contingencies.if: Active at Sun 16:50 CDMX and ESPN projects him two or more points above Kamara's 10.6
contingencies.then: Move Coker back into the FLEX before 18:20; otherwise Kamara stays

worthALook.name: DK Metcalf

case.label: The role

case.label: When to act

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be a handcuff to a player you already start, on a roster that needs a receiver first. On waivers until Wed 7 Oct, 01:00.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Dowdle practising in full on Wednesday with a coach saying the split returns: a second free Chem claim on Tuesday is then worth making, after the receiver.

case.label: What would change it

doNotChase.lead: The biggest riser among defences, and a point below the one you start.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 6 takeaways in three games, tied 3rd, and 7 and 9 points allowed the last two weeks (ChicagoBears.com); the Jets are without Hall, Mitchell, Taylor and their left guard, and Geno Smith was sacked five times in Week 3.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 7.8 against the Vikings' 8.9. The Jets have turned it over once all season, and Chicago start a backup quarterback behind a new left tackle.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Vikings defensive starter beyond Demmings scratched at 12:35.

doNotChase.name: Makai Lemon
doNotChase.lead: A rookie rising because two Eagles receivers are out. He runs the routes; someone else gets the ball.

case.label: The rise
case.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is out and expected to miss two or three games beyond today (Inquirer, 2 Oct); Hollywood Brown is out too. Lemon ran a route on 83.9% of dropbacks last week (FantasyPros, 4 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: A 10.2% target share and 0.45 yards per route (FantasyPros); 4, 1, 4 targets for 38 yards in three games (archive). Wicks is the one FantasyPros calls a flex, and Nicky Jam hold him. Lemon projects 10.5, a tenth under Kamara.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seven-plus targets against the Rams today: with Smith missing more games, he'd join Tuesday's comparison.

doNotChase.name: Malik Washington
doNotChase.lead: Miami's most-targeted receiver, in the league's lowest-scoring offence, against the defence you start.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 8, 5, 10 targets for 6.3, 8.7 and 11.1 points (archive); 12 catches for 152 yards, with four of 20-plus (Vikings.com preview).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 23 targets have produced 26.1 points (archive), from Malik Willis, whose 74.1 rating is fourth-worst among qualifiers; Miami average 12.0 points. He projects 10.3, under Kamara's 10.6.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Ten-plus targets and 15 points at Minnesota today: then he's compared with Metcalf and Boston on Tuesday for Monangai's seat.

doNotChase.name: Kalif Raymond
doNotChase.lead: A free agent producing every week, about to catch passes from his third quarterback in four games.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 9, 5, 7 targets for 16.4, 9.0 and 21.0 points (archive): a 20.4% target share and eight third-down catches, tied 2nd in the league (ChicagoBears.com; FantasyPros).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 9.8, below Kamara's 10.6. Tyson Bagent is expected to start, not Case Keenum, who threw him the Week 3 game, and Chicago's left tackle went on IR. The waiver tool didn't surface him.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A productive game from Bagent today: then he's part of Tuesday's comparison. He's a free agent, so nothing is lost by waiting.

waiverAnalysis.summary: One question, and it's an artefact: the tool counts the injured Jefferson as your weakest movable receiver, so Denzel Boston clears him. Three weeks of data, still thin. Nothing clears Monangai at running back. Same answer as Saturday.

rising.name: Denzel Boston
rising.roleReason: Cleveland's lead outside receiver: 95% of snaps, a route on 92% of dropbacks and 65% of the team's air yards on Thursday (RotoWire, 2 Oct, carried). The role is real. The comparison isn't: Jefferson's 3.0 in Week 3 is an ankle injury on his seventh snap.
rising.action: WATCH — on waivers until Wed 01:00 Mexico City; Tuesday's run compares him with Metcalf for Monangai's seat

settled.title: 'Don't move Coker out today' (Saturday afternoon's brief)
settled.result: Overnight Schefter reported he's unlikely to play and ESPN cut him to 0.0. The brief read Saturday's call-up as a hint, not a ruling. No points lost: the swap to Kamara is open until 18:20 tonight. Graded on tonight's and Monday's scores.

settled.title: 'McLaurin is expected to miss London' (Saturday afternoon's brief)
settled.result: Officially inactive this morning (CBS Sports' tracker). The swap away from him was already made.

settled.title: 'Wright limited Thursday' (Thursday afternoon's brief)
settled.result: He was upgraded to a full practice (FantasyPros, NBC, RotoWire, CBS, 1 Oct). The brief went out about an hour after the report. Gordon's row is corrected: it's a split.

settled.title: Coker in the flex over McLaurin (21 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Coker 3.8, McLaurin 19.7 on the bench. Closed WRONG. It was also a coin flip that should never have had a thesis.

settled.title: Hold Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 3.3 on 5 targets, so the under-six clause fired. Closed WRONG, not EXPIRED.

settled.title: Hold Pineiro over McPherson (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Pineiro 8, McPherson 11. The written falsifier didn't fire, so it stays open, but the hold lost 3 points.

settled.title: Start Warren over Tuten (13 Sep, reviewed weekly)
settled.result: Archive: 20.6 to 17.0 in Week 3; 2 of 3 weeks won. Closed RIGHT.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second TE (23 Sep)
Decline Jaxson Dart at 83% owned (23 Sep)
settled.result: Out for the season with knee damage (Bleacher Report, 28 Sep). Closed RIGHT.

cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Metcalf, Dowdle and Boston clear on Wed 7 Oct at 01:00 Mexico City; Meyers, Washington and Raymond are free agents anyone can add first. Footballers added Jaylen Wright on Saturday night.

cannotSee.body: wire_screen.py counts Week 4 as a stat week once one game is played, so its list is Steelers and Browns plus Tyler Higbee. Both passes returned the same eleven names as Saturday, so the verdicts are carried. It can't see Holani, Lemon, Washington or Raymond; they're in do-not-chase from the ownership column.

cannotSee.body: ESPN and CatCrave say knee; SI's Panthers site says hamstring. Either way he's on injured reserve for at least four games.
